questions.question: Who was appointed the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi in May 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinai Kumar Saxena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Delhi National Capital Territory's constitutional governor is the lieutenant governor.**
 
• On May 26, 2022, **Shri Vinai Kumar Saxena became the 22nd Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.**
 
• **Shri Saxena, 63, is the first corporate man** to be chosen for such a **gubernatorial position.**
 
• He has more than three decades of extensive expertise in the corporate and social sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Lieutenant Governor**

 
 
• **​**In the** Republic of India, a lieutenant governor is the constitutional head of five out of the eight union territories.**
 
• **The lieutenant governor is appointed by the President of India** for a term of five years and holds office at the President's pleasure.
 
• Since the union territories of Delhi, **Jammu, and Kashmir, and Puducherry** have a measure of self-government with an elected legislature and council of ministers, the role of the** lieutenant governor there is mostly a ceremonial one**, akin to that of a state's governor.
 
• In **Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Ladakh** however, the** lieutenant governor holds more power,** being both the head of state and head of government.

questions.question: Which of the following has unit m/s²?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration**

 
 
• **The rate at which an object's velocity with respect to time changes is referred to as acceleration**.
 
• A vector quantity is an acceleration (has magnitude and direction both).
 
• **LT-2 or meter per second square(m/s2) is the unit of acceleration.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed** 

 
 
• A scalar quantity, speed is defined as the **magnitude of the rate at which an object's position changes over time.**
 
• **The meter per second (m/s) or LT-1 unit of speed.**
 
 
 
• **Velocity**
 
 
• The pace at which **an object's position changes in relation to a frame of reference is known as its velocity, **which is a **time-dependent quantity.**
 
• A description of **an object's speed and direction of motion is what is meant by its velocity.**
 
• The quantity is a vector.
 
• **The meter per second (m/s) or LT-1 unit of velocity.**
 
 
 
• **Distance**
 
 
• The** International System of Units defines a meter** as the distance unit. It's interesting to note that many other derived units or quantities, such as volume, area, acceleration, and speed, may be constructed using this as the basic unit and a few formulae.
 
• **The meter(m) is the SI unit of length.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a unit of distance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Light year.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The **unit **of **length **used to express **astronomical distances **is the **light year**, which is roughly comparable to **5.88 trillion miles** or** 9.46 trillion kilometres.**
 
• According to the** International Astronomical Union (IAU),** a light-year is the distance that light travels in a vacuum in **one Julian year (365.25 days).**
 
• Since "light-year" incorporates the term "year," which designates a unit of measurement for time, it is occasionally misinterpreted as a** unit of time.**
 
• The light-year is most typically used to depict distances to stars and other distances on a** galactic scale**, especially in non-specialist contexts and popular science publications.
 
• The measuring unit most frequently used in professional astronomy is the **parsec**, which is derived from astrometry and equals **3.26 light-years. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Newton: **

 
 
• A **newton **is a unit of **force **in the International System of Units (symbol: N).
 
• **1 kgm/s²** is the force that accelerates a mass of** **one kilogramme** **by one metre per second square.
 
• It is named after **Isaac Newton.**
 
 
 
• **Watt:**
 
 
• **​**The **electrical power **determined in **Watts **is the equivalent of one ampere under one volt of pressure.
 
 
 
• **Joule:**
 
 
• **​**The **work performed **by a **force **of one newton acting through one metre is equivalent to one **joule**, a unit of work or energy in the International System of Units (SI).

questions.question: Which law, that was proposed in 1811, predicted that the same volume of gases at the same temperature and pressure would have the same number of molecules?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Avogadro’s law.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• **Avogadro proposed **in **1811 **that equal volumes of gases at the **same temperature **and **pressure** contain the same number of molecules.
 
• According to this **hypothesis**, the relative **molecular weights **of **any two gases **are the **same **as the **ratio **of their **densities **under the **same temperature **and **pressure **conditions.
 
• Avogadro also **correctly deduced **that **simple **gases were not made up of **solitary atoms**, but rather of compound molecules made up of two or more atoms.
 
• (Avogadro did not use the term "**atom**"; at the time, the terms "**atom**" and "**molecule**" were almost interchangeable. He mentioned three types of "**molecules**," one of which was a "elementary molecule"—what we would call an atom.)
 
• As a result, Avogadro was able to overcome the difficulty that **Dalton **and others had encountered when **Gay-Lussac **reported that the volume of water vapour above 100°C was twice the volume of oxygen used to form it.
 
• According to Avogadro, the **oxygen molecule split **into **two atoms **during the formation of water vapour.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Dalton’s law**

 
 
• ​The overall pressure exerted in a mixture of non-reacting gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the individual gases, according to **Dalton's law, **often known as** Dalton's law of partial pressures.** **John Dalton **discovered this empirical law in 1801 and made it public in 1802. The ideal **gas laws **are connected to **Dalton's law.**
 
 
 
• **Gay-Lussac’s law**
 
 
• ​A gas law known as **Gay-Lussac's law** asserts that a gas's pressure (when kept at a constant volume and mass) varies directly with its absolute temperature. In other words, while the mass is fixed and the volume is constant, the pressure a gas exerts is proportional to the temperature of the gas.
 
 
 
• **Charles' law**
 
 
• ​The experimental gas law known as **Charles' law**, commonly referred to as the law of volumes, illustrates how gases tend to expand when heated. **Charles's law** can now be stated as follows: When the pressure on a sample of a dry gas is held constant, the volume and **Kelvin temperature** will be in direct proportion.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasty was not the part of "Tripartite struggle", which fought for centuries to control over one particularly prized area Kanauj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kadamba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• 
 The **Tripartite Struggle**, also known as **Kannauj Triangle **Wars, took place in the ninth century between the **Pratihara Empire, the Pala Empire, and the Rashtrakuta Empire** for control of northern India.
 
 
• 
 However, **epigraphist Dineschandra **Sircar brought a new perspective to this conflict.
 
 
• 
 According to Sircar, the **conflict **between the **Pratihara Empire **and the **Rashtrakuta Empire **predated the **conflict **over** Kannauj State.**
 
 
• 
 In **Gujarat **and **Malwa **regions, these two powers shared a **common border**.
 
 
• 
 The shifting far from the permanent border caused **animosity **between the **two powers.**
 
 
• 
 **Dantidurga**, the founder of the Rashtrakuta Empire, had already defeated Nagabhata I of the Gurjara Pratihara dynasty, as evidenced by the **Dashavatara Temple **inscription of Dantidurga at Ellora and the Sghavarsha I, both belonging to Rashtrakuta dynasty.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

__
 
• **Rashtrakuta**

 
 
• **​**Between the sixth through the tenth centuries, the regal Indian dynasty known as **Rashtrakuta **ruled over a sizable portion of the Indian subcontinent. A copper plate grant from the seventh century is the first **Rashtrakuta inscription**, which describes their sovereignty over the **city of Manapur in Central or West India. **
 
 
 
• **Pala**
 
 
• Gopala __was the first ruler of the __Pala Dynasty.__
 
• Pala Dynasty was originated in the region of Bengal during the Late Classical Period of the Indian historical era.
 
• Palas followed the Mahayana and Tantric schools of Buddhism.
 
• It was founded by Gopala in 750CE.
 
• He was succeeded by Dharmapala.
 
 
 
• **Gurjara-Pratihara**
 
 
• ​A large portion of** Northern India** was governed by the **Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty **from the middle of the **eighth** to the **eleventh century.**
 
• First ruling in** Ujjain **and then in** Kannauj.** Arab troops that were approaching from the east of the Indus River were successfully halted by the **Gurjara-Pratiharas.**

questions.question: Which is the most popular coal in commercial use?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bituminous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• **Bituminous coal **is a **commercially **used type of coal. 
 
• Bituminous coal, also known as **black coal**, is a relatively soft coal that contains bitumen, a tar-like substance.
 
• This coal is classified according to its **plasticity**, **moisture content**, **volatility**, and **ash content**.
 
• Plasticity is required for the **production **of **coke**, which is used in the production of fuel gases such as producer gas.
 
• **Volatility **is critical for **steel production **and **power generation**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Anthracite:**

 
 
• **​**Anthracite, also known as a **hard **coal, and **a black coal, **is **hard**, compact variety of coal that has a submetallic lustre.
 
• It has the **highest carbon content**, the **fewest impurities**, and the **highest energy density **of any type of coal and is ranked first.
 
 
 
• **Peat:**
 
 
• Peat, also known as turf, is a type of **organic matter **that has partially decayed.
 
• **Turf **differs from peat in that it also refers to soil with grass.
 
• It can only be found in **peatlands, bogs, mires, moors, **or **muskegs.**
 
 
 
• **Lignite:**
 
 
• **​Lignite**, also known as **brown coal**, is a** soft, brown, combustible sedimentary rock** composed of naturally compressed peat.

questions.question: Mariana trench is located in which ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pacific ocean.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The **Mariana Trench **is the deepest oceanic trench on Earth, located in the western **Pacific Ocean **about 200 kilometres (124 miles) east of the Mariana Islands.
 
• It is **crescent**-**shaped **and approximately** 2,550 km (1,580 mi)** long and** 69 km (43 mi) wide.**
 
• The maximum known depth is **10,984 ± 25 metres​ **at the southern end of the Challenger Deep, a small slot-shaped valley in its floor.
 
• If Mount Everest were placed in the trench at this point, its peak would still be more than **2 kilometres underwater (1.2 mi).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Arctic ocean:**

 
 
• **​**The **Arctic Ocean **is the world's smallest and shallowest ocean, ranking fifth among the world's five major oceans.
 
• It is the coldest of all the oceans and covers an area of approximately** 14,060,000 km² (5,430,000 sq mi).**
 
• Although the** International Hydrographic Organization (IHO) **classifies it as an ocean, some oceanographers refer to it as the Arctic Mediterranean Sea.
 
 
 
• **Atlantic ocean:**
 
 
• With an area of approximately** 106,460,000 km²**, Atlantic Ocean is the** second-largest **of the world's five oceans (41,100,000 sq mi).
 
• It covers about** 20% **of **Earth's **surface and** 29%** of its **water **surface area.**​**
 
 
 
• **Southern ocean: **
 
 
• **​**The Southern Ocean, also known as the **Antarctic Ocean**, is the world's **southernmost ocean**, generally defined as being south of 60° S latitude and encircling Antarctica.

questions.question: What is the minimum quorum required in the Lok Sabha so that it can transact any business?

options.text: One-tenth of the total number of Members of the House
One-fourth of the total number of Members of the House
One-third of the total number of Members of the House
One-fifth of the total number of Members of the House

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-tenth of the total number of Members of the House.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Representatives of the **Lok Sabha **are **elected directly **by the **citizens **of **India**.
 
• **Members **of **parliament **are what they are called.
 
• **Members **of the **Rajya Sabha **are **elected **by **representatives **from **state legislative assemblies**.
 
• The **quorum **for Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha is the** one-tenth of each house's total membership.**
 
• If a **quorum **is **not present**, the house **cannot conduct **its **business**,** pass bills, or pass resolutions. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The **minimal number **of **participants **necessary for a meeting to start is known as a **quorum**.
 
• If a quorum is** ****not present**, it is the **Speaker's responsibility **to **adjourn **the House or **suspend **the **meeting **until a quorum is present.
 
• The **Constitution establishes **a **quorum.**
 
• Individual members have a** Five-year term.**
 
• **Casual vacancies, **when they occur, are filled through bye-elections for the remainder of the term.

questions.question: Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks are included in which measure of money supply?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**M2.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• 
 The total stock of money of all types (currency and demand deposits) held by the people of a country at a given point in time is referred to as the **money supply.**
 
 
• 
 Money supply can be measured in a variety of ways, including **M1, M2, M3, **and **M4 **measurements.
 
 
• 
 Every measurement has its own definition, with various components **ranging **from the **most liquid **to the **most rigid**.
 
 
• 
 Savings deposits at post office savings banks are included in the **M2 measurement **of money supply in India, making it a little more rigid than the** M1 measurement.**
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Money supply is defined as the **total amount **of **currency **that can be included in a country's economy.
 
• The total money supply includes both **cash **and **deposits **that can be** ****easily converted **into **cash**.
 
• Money supply economics is associated with **direct government **power because it is the government that issues currency, either in paper form or as a coin, as a combination of treasury bills and bank demand draughts.
 
• Similarly, **banks **have **influence **over the **money supply**, which they exercise through **reserves **and **credit controls**.
 
• Money supply has a significant **impact **on a **country's economy**.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the voting age reduced from 21 years to 18 years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1989**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On** December 6, 1988, the Lok Sabha **(the lower house of Parliament) approved the bill.
 
• On **December 7, 1988, the Rajya Sabha** (the upper house of Parliament) approved the bill.
 
• On** December 20, 1988, the bill received the President's assent and became the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act.**
 
• The amendment to** Article 326 of the Indian Constitution, which pertains to the right to vote, was made effective on March 28, 1989.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/246b3fc2e39ac4d19c5c8f4217ebe37fa2d58fcef7f20b59abe04fcf1e94747f.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 326 - The Constitution provides that the elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assembly of every State shall be on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
• Article 324 of the Indian Constitution deals it the power and authority to conduct, control, and supervise the entire election process in the country including elections to the Parliament, the Legislatures of every state, and to the offices of the President and Vice-President.

questions.question: Which sector was given the main emphasis in the second Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Industry__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industry sector** was given the main emphasis in the **second Five-Year Plan**.
 
• A part of the economy known as the industrial sector is made up of companies that help other companies with the **production, transportation, or manufacture of their goods.**
 
• Because the industrial sector sells its goods and services to other companies rather than to customers directly, it is referred to as a **secondary sector.**
 
• Due to its dependence on purchasing from **companies** in other sectors, the** industrial sector** is frequently driven by changes in **supply and demand** in other sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second Five-Year Plan**

 
 
• ​**April 1956 through March 1961 are included in the Second Five-Year Plan.**
 
• The second strategy involved setting India up for industrialization.
 
• The **architect** of the second five-year plan was **P.C. Mahalanobis.**
 
• He gave the industrial foundation of the economy the most attention.
 
• In light of this, the **1948 Industrial Policy Resolution** was revised, and a new resolution was adopted in 1956.

questions.question: Which Indian tabla virtuoso and musician won the 'Best Contemporary World Music Album' Grammy award for 'Global Drum Project'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ustad Zakir Hussain.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Zakir Hussain**

 
 
• ​The **Indian tabla virtuoso and musician who won the 'Best Contemporary World Music Album' Grammy award for 'Global Drum Project'** was **Ustad Zakir Hussain.**
 
• Ustad Zakir Hussain, an Indian tabla musician, composer, percussionist, music producer, and film actor, was born on **March 9, 1951.**
 
• The Indian government honoured him with the **Padma Shri in 1988, the Padma Bhushan in 2002, and the Padma Vibhushan in 2023.**
 
• Also, he received the **Ratna Sadsya in 2018**, the Fellowship of the **Sangeet Natak Akademi, and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Prize** from the Government of India in 1990. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Drum Project**

 
 
• **Mickey Hart, Zakir Hussain, Sikiru Adepoju, and Giovanni Hidalgo** collaborated on the album titled **World Drum Project.**
 
• The album includes music made with a variety of **drums and other instruments,** vocals from people chanting and singing, and electronic samples.
 
• It combines traditional music with contemporary electronic music, which was informed by **Mickey Hart's musicological research** on drumming from throughout the world.
 
• The **2009 Grammy Award for Best Contemporary World Music Album** went to Global Drum Project.

questions.question: In leaves transpiration takes place through ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stomata.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stomata**

 
 
• In leaves transpiration takes place through **stomata**.
 
• The little **apertures** known as stomata are found on the **epidermis of leaves**.
 
• **Stomata** are visible under a **light microscope.**
 
• Stomata can be found on the **stems and other portions** of various plants.
 
• In **gaseous exchange and photosynthesis,** stomata are crucial. Via opening and closing, they regulate the **rate of transpiration.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transpiration**

 
 
• Water is lost from the **aerial regions of plants **in the form of water vapour through a **biological process called transpiration.**
 
• Like all other living things, plants need an **excretory system** to remove extra water from their bodies.
 
• **Transpiration** is the term for this process of removing extra water from the body of the plant. Typically, it is the** evaporation of water from the leaf surface.**
 
• The plants only use a small portion of the water they absorb for **growth and development**.

questions.question: Who was recognised as ‘Asthana Nartaki’ (resident dancer) of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam for her contribution in the development and promotion of the Indian classical dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yamini Krishnamurthy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yamini Krishnamurthy**

 
 
• ​**Yamini Krishnamurthy** was recognised as ‘**Asthana Nartaki’** (resident dancer) of the **Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam** for her contribution in the development and promotion of the **Indian classical dance forms.**
 
• Mungara Yamini Krishnamurthy, an Indian dancer who specialises in **Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam, was born on December 20, 1940.**
 
• In Madras, Yamini Krishnamurthy made his **debut in 1957.**
 
• She holds the **honour of being the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam's Asthana Nartaki (resident dancer). **
 
• The **Padma Shree (1968), Padma Bhushan (2001), and Padma Vibhushan (2016)**, three of the highest civilian honours bestowed by the Republic of India, were among the many honours she received for her dancing career.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Afterwards, she received training from illustrious teachers like **Thanjavur Kittappa Pillai and Kanchipuram Ellappa Pillai.**
 
• Under the instruction of **Vedantam Lakshmi Narayana Shastri, Chinta Krishnamurthy, and Pasumarthy Venugopal Krishna Sharma,** she learned Kuchipudi.
 
• Yamini studied Odissi under **Guru Pankaj Charan Das and Kelucharan Mahapatra** in addition to Bharatnatyam and Kuchipudi.

questions.question: Manimekalai describes the story of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kovalan and Madhavi’s Daughter.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kovalan and Madhavi’s Daughter**

 
 
• ​**Manimekalai** describes the story of **Kovalan and Madhavi’s Daughter.**
 
• The daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi, who takes after her mother's career as a dancer and Buddhist nun, is also known by the name Manimekalai.
 
• **Kulavanikan Seethalai Sataar **penned the **Tamil-Buddhist epic Manimekalai** in the sixth century.
 
• It is an "**anti-love narrative**" that includes some of the heroes and their offspring from the "l**ove romance**" in the first Tamil epic **Silappadikaram**.
 
• The epic contains 30 cantos and 4,861 lines in the akaval metre.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of the only three of **Tamil literature's Five Great Epics** to have endured to the present day is the **Manimekalai**.
 
• The Manimekalai and its** twin-epic Silappadikaram** are both recognised as important works of literature that shed light on Tamil regions' (**India and Sri Lanka's**) way of **life, culture, and civilization** in the first centuries of the Common Era.

questions.question: “A History of British India” is a work Published by ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James Mill.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Mill**

 
 
• ​**“A History of British India” is a work Published by James Mill.**
 
• James Mill was a **Scottish historian, economist, political theorist, and philosopher **who lived from **6 April 1773 to 23 June 1836**.
 
• He is one of the founding members of the **Ricardian school of economics**.
 
• He was one of the famous **historians who adopted a colonial viewpoint**, and he also produced The History of British India (1817).
 
• He was the first author to divide Indian history into three distinct periods: **Hindu, Muslim, and British.**
 
• This division has proven to be extremely influential in the field of Indian historical research.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A History of British India**

 
 
• **​James Mill,** a Scottish historian, economist, political theorist, and philosopher, chronicled the history of Company rule in India in his three-volume masterpiece **The History of British India.**
 
• When it was initially **published in 1817,** the book was an immediate hit and brought Mill "**a measure of affluence**."
 
• In accordance with the prominent **political forces and their religious ties**, Mill divided Indian history into the **Hindu, Muslim, and British periods**.
